title: 4. Qualifications and Disqualifications of Assembly Members

blocks.content: The decision of the Governor on questions as to disqualification of members shall be final, after obtaining the opinion of the Election Commission.

rows: Speaker of the Assembly / Chairman of Council
No advisory body required; Speaker decides directly
Office of profit, unsound mind, insolvency, criminal conviction
Voluntarily giving up party membership, voting against party whip

items: Minimum age limit differs: 25 years for Legislative Assembly (MLA) vs 30 years for Legislative Council (MLC).
Disqualification under Constitutional/RPA grounds is decided by the Governor (on ECI opinion), whereas Anti-Defection disqualification is decided solely by the Speaker/Chairman.
A person convicted and sentenced to imprisonment for not less than 2 years is disqualified from the date of conviction and remains disqualified for 6 years after release.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 173 specifies that a person must be a citizen of India and at least 25 years old to be qualified for election to the Legislative Assembly.
A candidate must subscribe to an oath or affirmation before an authorized representative of the Election Commission of India.
Under Article 191, grounds for disqualification include holding an office of profit, being of unsound mind, undischarged insolvency, or acquiring foreign citizenship.
Disqualification under the Representation of the People Act (1951) includes conviction for offences resulting in imprisonment for two or more years.
The Governor decides on disqualification questions under constitutional grounds upon obtaining the mandatory opinion of the Election Commission.
Disqualification on the grounds of defection under the Tenth Schedule is determined by the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly.
